answer: The verdict is "not_fit", with confidence 0.75. It has no conditions: the conditions list is empty, which fits a not_fit verdict. The review says the design is "not fit to start building" because one critical finding, FND-006 (the Redis idempotency fast path is not scoped to the merchant), and about ten high findings break objectives the document makes binding. What the review gives instead is what would move the verdict to fit_with_conditions. That means fixing FND-006, FND-043 and FND-037 (idempotency and recovery), FND-033 (the Fraud Hook's PAN detokenisation), FND-035 and FND-009 (late-approval reversal and the latency budget), FND-037 and FND-036 (RPO and HSM/DR), FND-040 (the 08:00 SGT reconciliation deadline), FND-010 (fraud scoring at launch) and FND-041 (payout account controls). The review notes that confidence is lowered for FND-021, FND-038 and FND-030 because no external research was possible (DEG-002).

answer: The top-ranked finding is FND-006 (rank 1, critical). Its title is "Redis idempotency fast path is not merchant-scoped and skips the body-hash check". The review recommends changing the Redis key in §9.2 and §24 to idem:resp:{merchant_id}:{idempotency_key}. The request_hash would be stored with the cached response and compared on every hit, with a 422 returned on mismatch. It also recommends extending the FR-5 test in §26.1 with two cases: two merchants using the same key, and a fast-path hit with a different body. The expected benefit is that "FR-5 holds on every path" and responses can't leak across merchants. The recommendation names four supporting evidence entries. EV-018 is the key format idem:resp:{idempotency_key}. EV-019 is P3's (merchant, key) scoping. EV-020 says merchants' own order or invoice numbers are accepted as keys. EV-047 is an inference from those three. The finding also cites EV-004 and EV-099.
